details.d: Welcome to the City of Brotherly Love, Philadelphia! Moishe House Philly is the place to be for Jewish 20-somethings and their friends. Our monthly seven events are both in our house (Shabbat potluck anyone??) and around the city (Moishe Eats Series!). We work with our community to learn with local rabbi's and visionaries, and throw some humongous Hannuka and Purim parties at local venues. Whether you're looking for a homey night in with good food and a movie, or a rockin' dance party with a DJ in the kitchen, we've got it! We're a pluralistic, welcoming, accepting, and inclusive space for young Jews to connect over common ground. Philly never felt so good!

details.d: Montefiore Cemetery has been owned and operated by the same family since 1910. Montefiore is a Jewish cemetery with a perpetual charter. Our cemetery is widely considered one of the most stately and dignified Jewish cemeteries in the area. At Montefiore we believe in honoring the past and providing for the future, because a life well-lived is an everlasting memory. To perpetuate the memories of those whose final resting place is at Montefiore, we have planned meaningful development for the future. The future at Montefiore focuses on servicing your family’s needs throughout the 21st century and beyond. This includes space availability for the generations to come and, of course, meticulous maintenance and constant upgrading of our facilities. Montefiore is centrally located, for convenient access, in nearby Jenkintown, PA.

details.d: Spruce Street Minyan is a vibrant, traditional, and egalitarian minyan for young professionals and graduate students (in their 20s and 30s) living in Philadelphia. We host a monthly Friday night service in a community space, followed by a delicious, home-cooked Shabbat potluck. We aim to connect identifying, searching, intentional Jews for meaningful davening. We hope that through this monthly minyan, we can build a powerful community of energized and committed folks who love celebrating some of the best parts of our tradition: spirituality and food! Our minyan is grassroots and homegrown, and we intend on keeping it that way!
